history.dynasty: Chola and Pandya periods (inscriptions); local legend credits a Sivalaya Chola
history.period: Inscriptions: one dated Kaliyuga year 1641 (~357 years old), another ~600 years old recording the place as Pidariyur; the current front temple built from 1948; legendary age ~3000 years (unverified - treat as legend); one travel account dates the hill temple to the 9th-century Chola period (verify)
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: the temple is NOT in Erode city - it crowns the hill above Chennimalai town, about 25-30 km south of Erode (CSV town 'Erode' refers to the district/nearest big city; corrected to Chennimalai). Documented with the corrected location. The Chennimalai Murugan Temple is a famous Kongu Nadu hill temple of Subramanya, ~400 m (1749 ft) above sea level, reached by 1320-1330 steps or a motorable road with hairpin bends (temple buses run to the top). Core legend: a landowner's black cow (Karam Pasu) discharged its milk daily at one spot; digging 5-6 ft down revealed a beautiful Muruga idol sculpted only to the hip - when an artisan's first chisel drew blood, the landlord took it as divine will and consecrated the idol as Dandayudapani on the hill, where the lower half remains rough to this day. The hill's origin legend mirrors Tiruchengode: in a strength contest between Vayu (wind god) and Adi Seshan (serpent king), a peak of the Himalayas/Mahameru flew off and fell here; hence its names Makutagiri (Krita yuga, worshipped by Vishnu), Kanakagiri (Treta yuga, worshipped by Lakshmi), Pushpagiri (Dwapara yuga, worshipped by the Ashta Durgas), and in this aeon Siragiri/Chennimalai, worshipped by Siddhars. Other legends: King Sivalaya Chola was relieved of Brahmahatti dosha when Muruga appeared as an archakar and worshipped himself; princesses Amirthavalli and Sundaravalli did penance here to be reborn as Valli and Devasena; Arunagirinathar sang of this abode (Kundruthoradal), and Kanda Sashti Kavasam was staged here. The moolavar is equated with Sevvai (Mars), the other eight planets encircling him - circumambulating the Lord is believed to equal a navagraha circumambulation. Pinnakku Siddhar, one of the 18 Siddhars, lived in the hill cave, said to connect by underground passage to the Bhogar Siddhar cave at Palani. At the foothills stands the Kailasanathar Temple, the scene of the annual festival. name: Chennimalai Murugan Temple
town: Chennimalai (CSV town 'Erode' is approximate - the temple is on the hill above Chennimalai town, ~28-30 km from Erode city)
town_description: Chennimalai, the 'Handloom Town' of Erode district, lies about 28-30 km from Erode city near Perundurai. It is famed for its handloom weaving and the 1700-acre Chennimalai hill rising above the town - home to peacocks, monkeys and medicinal herbs, with the Murugan temple on top and a 1320-step climb (or motorable road) to the summit.

travel.railway: Ingoor (Ingur) station - about 7.5 km; Perundurai and Erode Junction also serve (verify).
travel.road: From Erode via Perundurai; Devasthanam buses run from the foothill to the hilltop; motorable road with hairpin bends; ~1320 steps for climbers (verify).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; evenings are pleasant on the hilltop (per visitor reviews).
